headline: How Amul turned *daily news* into free advertising

slides.title: It started in *1966*
slides.body: Amul and its ad agency created the little girl in the polka-dot dress, and began putting her on billboards that reacted to that week's news.

slides.title: Why it *still works*
slides.body: Speed: the ad lands while the news is hot. Humour: people share a good pun. One mascot: decades of attention build on the same character.

cta.title: Be fast. Be funny. Be consistent.
cta.body: Moment marketing doesn't need a big budget. It needs a recognisable voice that shows up when people are already talking.

caption:
60 years. One little girl in a polka-dot dress. Zero chasing trends — she IS the trend. 🧈

Since 1966, Amul's topical billboards have reacted to the week's news with a pun — fast, funny and always on-brand. That's moment marketing before the term existed.

Which Amul topical is your all-time favourite? 👇

headline: Cadbury used AI to make *Shah Rukh Khan* advertise your local kirana store
caption:
Shah Rukh Khan, brand ambassador for… your neighbourhood kirana store? 🤯

For Diwali 2021, Cadbury Celebrations and Ogilvy used AI to let small local shops create their own ad featuring SRK — naming their store, so the ads could run in their own area. Big brand, local heart.

Would this work for brands today? 👇

caption:

headline: Before Nokia made phones, it was a *paper mill*
caption:
Before Nokia made the phone your dad still swears by, it made… paper. 📄

Nokia began in 1865 as a paper mill in Finland. Over 150 years it moved through rubber boots, cables and electronics before becoming a mobile phone giant.
